children: Main Street Capital’s investment income rose 2% year over year, while net investment income declined 3% and the increase in net assets from operations fell 5%. Higher interest income and lower investment-income taxes partly offset higher expenses, including interest expense, and lower dividend income; net realized losses also increased.
² Reported as “NET INCREASE IN NET ASSETS RESULTING FROM OPERATIONS”. ³ Reported as “NET INCREASE IN NET ASSETS RESULTING FROM OPERATIONS PER SHARE—BASIC AND DILUTED”.
: Interest income increased 8% to $111.9M, primarily on higher average income-producing debt investments, partly offset by lower benchmark rates and non-accrual investments.
: Dividend income fell 18%, primarily reflecting a $6.9M decrease from LMM portfolio companies.
: Annualized total return on investments was 14.8%, compared with 16.9% in the year-earlier quarter.
: Non-accrual investments were $54.7M at fair value, or 0.9% of the Investment Portfolio at fair value, as of September 30, 2026.
